title: Village notes
subtitle: Short notes on the four villages of the Sample River Basin
author: Sample field team
notice: Synthetic example, not real data. Ardena, Belmora, Corvel and Dunhal are fictional villages.

chapters.title: Ardena
chapters.description: Head end of the main canal.

sections.title: A piped supply on an expired permit
sections.body: The village government runs a small piped supply from the river to a storage tank. The abstraction permit shown to the team had expired, yet everyone involved treats the use as lawful. The FAO typology calls this **assumed** tenure: a formal right wrongly assumed to exist because of the official character of the user.

sections.title: Fishing below the weir
sections.body: Residents fish in the pool below the weir throughout the year. No water or fisheries rule addresses the practice, so it is recorded as **unrecognised** tenure.

chapters.title: Belmora
chapters.description: Middle reach of the main canal.

sections.title: Dug wells
sections.body: Most households draw water from shallow dug wells without a permit or registration. Only one source describes the practice, so the record is graded *single-source* until a second source confirms it.

images.caption: Household dug well (placeholder illustration, synthetic example)

sections.title: A brick works with a permit
sections.body: A brick works holds a long-term abstraction permit for its borehole: a **modern permit-based** right, separate from land. It is the only record of this type in the sample.

chapters.title: Corvel
chapters.description: Tail end of the main canal.

sections.title: Water that arrives late
sections.body: Corvel's farmers hold land-based rights in the scheme but report that water rarely reaches them after the wet season. See the main story for the pumping that fills the gap.

sections.title: The wetland
sections.body: Households cut reeds in the wetland below the drain outlet. The record is marked *aggregate only*, so its position on the map is generalized.

chapters.title: Dunhal
chapters.description: Upland hamlet, not served by the canal.

sections.title: Turns on the spring channel
sections.body: Upland farmers take turns on the channel below Ridge Spring in an order set by the customary steward. The rotation is recorded as **customary** tenure, separate from the household use of the spring itself.

sections.title: An unregistered pump group
sections.body: A group of farmers shares one pump on Ridge Brook. The group is not registered and has no legal personality, so it cannot hold a permit in its own name. The FAO typology calls this **impossible** tenure: a formal right is legally impossible for the presumed holder.
